text:
Alex C: raising S-812 — customer reports an unexpected KMS decrypt. looking at our audit stream the decrypt event has no principal_id, can someone help reconstruct who triggered it?

Nina R: @Alex C can you paste the raw audit line so we can see fields?

Alex C: sure, here's the event we ingested:```{
  "timestamp": "2026-11-03T14:12:17Z",
  "event_type": "kms.decrypt",
  "key_id": "rw-crypto",
  "result": "success",
  "request_id": "req-9a8b7c",
  "resource": "customer-789/model-checkpoint",
  "principal_id": null,
  "caller_ip": "34.56.78.90"
}```

Pradeep K: missing principal_id is the core problem. historically we allowed nullable principal_id for internal proxyed calls. did we roll any RBAC / proxy changes recently that could strip identity?

Jen M: we merged the internal-proxy RBAC refactor on 2026-10-28 — changelog note here: https://git.internal/redwood/internal-proxy/changeset/458. that PR changed how we forward auth headers. could be related.

Sam T: incident-bot: created incident S-812 from alert 'kms-decrypt-unexpected'

Nina R: can we correlate cloud provider KMS access logs with request_id and caller_ip? provider logs usually contain the caller principal even if our ingest pipeline lost it.

Alex C: running a quick provider query: `/logs query 'request_id=req-9a8b7c' --project customer-789` returned an entry showing `svc-inference-proxy@redwood-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com` as the caller. putting that here because it doesn't match the customer principal.

Pradeep K: that service account should only access model-serving resources. need to check whether a policy binding accidentally granted it access to customer-789 storage. I'll look at IAM policy history and policy-bindings audit.

Jen M: I'll pull the RBAC proxy PR diff and the deploy timeline. if the proxy started dropping x-forwarded-principal header we would lose principal_id during ingestion.

Alex C: schema proposal (for discussion): make `principal_id` non-null for all `kms.decrypt` events; add fields `principal_type` and `principal_email`; add `kek_key_id` capturing the customer KMS key resource; and emit `auth_chain` array when requests are proxied. This will help downstream reconstructions.

Nina R: +1 to schema changes. also propose a customer-facing validation script that: 1) pulls provider KMS logs for given time range 2) matches on request_id/caller_ip/key_id 3) outputs a CSV with columns [timestamp, key_id, request_id, our_principal, provider_principal, matched(boolean)]. useful for legal/forensics.

Sam T: created task INFRA-2347 to update audit-schema and INFRA-2348 for the validation script. assigning INFRA-2347 to @Pradeep K and INFRA-2348 to @Jen M. ETA 48h for initial changes.

Pradeep K: I'll also run a backfill plan: scan last 30 days for decrypt events with null principal_id, attempt to map via request_id to provider logs and populate `principal_id` in the audit-store. will log how many we can map vs unknown.

Jen M: I'll add a canary to the RBAC proxy so it includes `x-forwarded-principal` and a `x-proxy-trace` id on every proxied request. will add an acceptance test that verifies these headers make it into the audit event.

Alex C: action items summary: 1) provider correlation to identify actual actor (Pradeep+Nina) 2) update audit schema + roll out ingest validation (Pradeep+Jen) 3) backfill last 30 days where possible (Pradeep) 4) add canary header and test in proxy (Jen) 5) produce customer CSV for disclosure if needed (Nina). I'll update incident S-812 with timeline and findings as we go.

Nina R: pinging @legal and @support to prepare a disclosure template if we need to notify the customer :eyes: 

Pradeep K: starting correlation now, will post progress here.

Jen M: quick note — if we change the schema to require `principal_id` for decrypts, we need a graceful migration for older events and a feature flag in ingest to enforce validation after rollout.

Alex C: good catch. make validation behind feature flag and enable after backfill completes.

Sam T: :thumbsup:
